clue.text: Go off, missing entrance to pass

indicators.note: missing its entrance means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a saddle is a low pass or col between two peaks

explanation.surface: Someone sets off on a journey but cannot find the way into a mountain pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go off' is the definition, as eggs go off; the pass is a SADDLE, and 'missing entrance to' drops its first letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs that addle have gone rotten, the sense of spoiling food.

clue.text: Old country — one invested in freely by Asians

indicators.note: invested in places one letter inside the rearranged group
freely means the letters are arranged loosely

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single investment was made generously by Asian businessmen in a former nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' is the anagram signal and 'invested in' the container: one is put inside the rearranged letters, with ABYSSANS shuffled round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Former name of Ethiopia, the East African empire.

clue.text: Order upset staff in charge

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: A manager's command throws the staff into confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: The Doric is one of the classical architectural styles of columns.

clue.text: Perfume's indispensable quality

explanation.definitionFit: It means both a concentrated fragrance and the intrinsic nature of a thing.

clue.text: Antelope I caught on both sides of an island

indicators.note: on both sides of means the pair stands at either end of the antelope
both asks for the pair of letters to be used twice over

parts.note: taken as written
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: A hunter bags an antelope on an island, with prey on either side.
explanation.walkthrough: IC goes on both sides of ELAND: IC + ELAND + IC. 'of an island' is an adjectival definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things belonging to the North Atlantic nation of Reykjavik.

clue.text: Stupidity of one officer seen in amateurish housework

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: seen in places the officer inside the housework

parts.note: DIY is do-it-yourself, home improvements done by amateurs

explanation.surface: A soldier is caught doing clumsy repairs around the home.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolishness or extreme silliness.

clue.text: Cosmetic coming from East on the old ship

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of the
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: Make-up arrives from the Orient aboard a vintage vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Makeup applied to outline the lashes.

clue.text: Rent land from a northern city

indicators.note: land from means that word is taken away from the city

parts.note: Sunderland is a city in north-east England
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ground is let out from a city in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money for a lease but is the past participle of rend, torn apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Torn apart into pieces.

clue.text: Acting in time to undermine underworld infamy

indicators.note: in a down clue, to undermine means to go below

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the realm itself

indicators.note: in places the acting word inside the time

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time
on means acting, as on stage

explanation.surface: Performing to sabotage the criminal fraternity brings disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Shame or disgrace.

clue.text: Extract from epic I tediously quoted

indicators.note: Extract from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone quotes a passage from a boring epic poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Referred to or mentioned as evidence.

clue.text: Pay to follow bowls in county, once

indicators.note: to follow puts the payment after the bowling

parts.note: to york a batsman is to bowl him with a yorker in cricket
to hire is to pay for the use of

explanation.surface: A bowls player in a shire is paid after playing.
explanation.walkthrough: A yorker is a cricket delivery pitched at the batsman's feet; to york is to bowl one. The county was split into separate counties in 1974, hence 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: It was England's largest historic shire until local government reorganisation broke it up.

clue.text: Disturbance in university class

parts.note: being up means in residence at a university, especially Oxford or Cambridge
a set is a class or group of pupils

explanation.surface: A student causes a commotion in a university lecture.
explanation.walkthrough: To be 'up' at Oxford or Cambridge is to be in residence there.
explanation.definitionFit: An upset is a disruption or commotion, as of a stomach or plans.

clue.text: Support minor poet in dotage

parts.note: to second a proposal is to support it
a minor is a child, someone under age
Thomas Hood was a 19th-century English poet

explanation.surface: Someone backs a young poet who is elderly and failing.
explanation.definitionFit: Senility in old age is often likened to a return to infancy.

clue.text: Less sensible collection

definitions.meaning: more numb, having less feeling or sensation
a ... of things is a group or collection of them

explanation.walkthrough: 'sensible' here means able to feel sensation, so 'less sensible' is more numb, not more foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Numb lacks feeling, so its comparative is less feeling; a number is also a group or batch.

clue.text: Nut much food made in Silicon Valley?

definitions.text: Nut much food made in Silicon Valley

parts.words: Nut much food made in Silicon Valley
parts.note: a tiny fried potato piece, read as the tech product of California

explanation.definitionFit: A tiny integrated circuit used in computers.

clue.text: Reportedly display weaving machine, an old family possession

a loom is the frame on which cloth is woven

explanation.surface: A weaving loom, displayed proudly, has been in the family for generations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' makes the display word a homophone: the sound of it gives a word spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a treasured object is handed down through generations of relatives.

clue.text: Hired soldier shows forbearance about near-disaster

parts.note: mercy is forbearance from punishment

indicators.note: disaster signals the letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A hired soldier shows clemency after a close shave.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier fighting for pay.

clue.text: Singular vessels appearing in drawings

parts.note: ketches are two-masted sailing boats

explanation.surface: Lone boats feature in pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough drawings or outlines.

clue.text: Nobleman making mischievous notes about this country

for a British newspaper this country is the UK

explanation.surface: A peer writes cheeky remarks about Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: An archduke was a high-ranking prince, especially of the Austrian royal house.

clue.text: See side assembled outside old church

assembled means the letters are put together in another order

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Look at a group gathered outside an ancient church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembled' rearranges SIDE into DISE, which goes round OCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's see is the district under the bishop's authority.

clue.text: Moneylender bound to be in the old city

indicators.note: to be in places the certain word inside the ancient city

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A moneylender is certain to be found in the historic part of town.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurer lends cash at excessive interest rates.

clue.text: Imagine setting out up-river in a certain direction

in places the upward river inside the compass point

parts.note: SSE is south-south-east, a compass direction
taken as written
the Po is a river in Italy

explanation.surface: Picture setting off upstream on a particular course.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume or think something likely.

clue.text: Extremely tame sort of jazz group

parts.note: trad is traditional jazz

explanation.surface: A gentle style of jazz band plays.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a tetrad is any set or collection of four things, like a quartet.

clue.text: Dim new lot to shake up in new form

indicators.note: in new form says these letters are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A slow-witted person is told to reorganise a new batch of things.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is all fifteen letters of 'new lot to shake up'; the second 'new' belongs to the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dim is slow to understand, failing to grasp ideas quickly.

clue.text: A cooker knocked out of shape

definitions.meaning: past tense of stave, staved in or dented

explanation.definitionFit: Both a kitchen range and the past tense of stave, to dent inwards.

clue.text: Nimble priest leaves in a weakened physical state

indicators.note: leaves means the priest departs from the word

parts.note: fragile means frail or delicate
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest

explanation.surface: An agile clergyman departs when frail.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick and light in movement.

clue.text: Pigment companion found in mineral aggregate

parts.note: ore is rock from which metal is extracted
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A geologist and companion discover pigment in a rock deposit.
explanation.definitionFit: This earthy yellow-brown clay is used as a colouring in paints.

clue.text: Girl on instrument — not piano, a different one

indicators.note: in an across clue, on places the girl after the instrument
not piano means the letter for piano is removed

parts.note: the harp is a stringed instrument
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
Monica is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl plays a harp, then switches to something other than the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not piano' drops the musical P from the instrument; 'on' puts the girl after it. 'a different one' means a different instrument from the harp.
explanation.definitionFit: The mouth organ is a separate musical device from the harp.

clue.text: Communicated with paper boy

parts.note: the Daily Express is a British newspaper
Ed is a boy's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A message was passed on via a paperboy.
explanation.definitionFit: To put feelings into words is to convey or state them.

clue.text: Abrasive agent on the board?

parts.note: reads like a harsh member of a company board, but is the gritty coating of a nail file
